احتياج النيتروجين ممكن يكون مهمًا، لكن مفيش نقص أو كمية اتثبتت.

فكّر في تنقيط مصمم ومراقَب؛ مفيش دورة ري أسبوعية أو مرتين في الأسبوع تصلح للجميع.

استخرج الكمية من احتياج المحصول والتحليل والإرشاد المحلي، مش من عبارة «قليل ومتكرر» فقط.
اربط الإضافة بالنمو والاحتياج المقاس؛ التسميد كل أسبوع أو كل أسبوعين مش قاعدة عامة.
لو منتج ذائب معتمد والمعدات مناسبة، أوصله مع تنقيط مفحوص لمنطقة الجذور؛ وإلا اختار بديلًا صالحًا.

units.delivery: اتكلم بالمصري القاهري الطبيعي، كأنك مدرّس بيشرح لطلبة تعليم فني زراعي بهدوء ووضوح. الجيم مصرية زي G في gold، والقاف همزة في الكلمات اليومية اللّي المصريين بينطقوها كده. نبرة دافية وسرعة متوسّطة ووقفات طبيعية. راعي الشدّات من غير مبالغة أو تطويل. حافظ على كلّ النفي والشروط وحدود التدريب. اقرأ نصّ الإلقاء بسّ، من غير مقدّمة أو تعليق أو قراءة التعليمات. بلاش فصحى أو لهجة خليجية أو نبرة نشرات الأخبار. اشرح النص كله كجزء واحد متصل، من غير تمثيل شخصيات أو إضافة نصايح طبية.

sourceBindings.text: الحالة ٤: ذرة صغيرة بنفسجية في طين بارد
ذرة صغيرة ورقها بنفسجي ونموها بطيء في ربيع بارد على تربة طينية ثقيلة.
البرودة أو البلل أو ضعف التجذير ممكن يحد امتصاص P حتى لو P كافي في التربة.
نقص P حقيقي أو سبب آخر يفضل احتمالًا.
افحص الحرارة والصرف ونمو الجذور وتحليل P مناسبًا، وهل تتحسن الذرة لما التربة تدفى.
ما تزودش ماء تلقائيًا لتربة طينية باردة ومبلولة؛ افحص الرطوبة والصرف الأول.
DAP أو فوسفات أحادي الأمونيوم MAP أمثلة محتملة لمصدر P، بس بعد التأكد من الاحتياج الزراعي وملاءمة المنتج.
استند للتحليل وإرشاد محلي للمحصول، مش «كمية بسيطة» مبهمة.
خطط للوقت المناسب لاحتياج P وظروف آمنة؛ بلاش علاج فوري من غير فحص.

الشريط قرب الجذور الصغيرة ممكن يناسب مع بعد آمن عن البذرة حسب المنتج، ومش متفوق في كل ظرف على البدائل. المثال التعليمي ده بيوضح شريط سماد بادئ وقت الزراعة على بُعد 2 بوصة جنب صف البذور و2 بوصة تحته. ده مثال لطريقة الوضع، مش ضبط ثابت لكل الحالات ولا تعليمات نحفر جنب شتلات قائمة. الوضع الفعلي يتحدد بتعليمات المنتج والمحصول والمعدات وإرشاد محلي يحافظ على سلامة البذور.
اختبر فرضية P وظروف التربة قبل توصية تسميد بأربع قرارات.

sourceBindings.text: Case 1: sandy tomato patch
Hot, windy sandy plot with flood/surface watering; tomatoes look well in the morning but wilt in the afternoon and older leaves are pale or yellow.
High daytime demand may exceed short-term root uptake; limited root-zone storage or poorly controlled flood application may contribute.
Older-leaf yellowing raises mobile N or K shortage, leaching, root problems or another cause.
Sample moisture through the root zone in morning and afternoon; inspect roots, drainage, timing of previous watering, weather and emitter feasibility.
Obtain soil/tissue nutrient evidence and a crop-stage record before selecting a fertilizer.

Consider a filtered, maintainable drip system over uncontrolled flood delivery for the stated site, while measuring its operation; do not prescribe daily watering from appearance alone. Near-root delivery avoids overhead spray drift, can reduce soil-surface evaporation and inter-row weed wetting, and can keep foliage drier to reduce some disease risk. Small monitored applications can suit limited sandy storage, but excess can still pass below roots; these benefits depend on design, operation and conditions.
Choose a tomato-appropriate nutrient source only after evidence; a balanced soluble product is one possible product class, not a diagnosis.
Use test results, plant demand, current supply and local guidance; no number follows from the leaf colour.
Match confirmed demand and loss risk; fertigation every watering or every other watering is not an automatic schedule.
Use product-approved root-zone delivery if fertigation is justified; monitor leaching and uniformity.
The teaching model discusses a fruiting-stage tomato fertilizer class. Confirm the actual stage before using that example; the bank question alone does not supply a fertilizer analysis.
Separate heat/water and nutrient hypotheses, verify both, then choose a conditional water and 4R plan.

sourceBindings.text: Case 2: stunted wheat in wet clay
After heavy rain the clay field has standing water; wheat is stunted and some older leaf margins yellow.
Waterlogging can deprive roots of oxygen and reduce water or nutrient uptake.
K shortage is possible from marginal symptoms, but root stress, other nutrient disorders or damage can mimic it.
Map standing water and drainage, examine roots when safe and reassess after drainage; obtain soil/tissue K evidence if symptoms persist.
Check whether feasible temporary surface drainage is safe and permitted at this site; plan longer-term drainage only after site evaluation.
Stop added irrigation while the soil is saturated and prioritise drainage assessment; do not claim that every clay field should avoid all irrigation forever.
Only select a K source such as potassium sulfate if a need is established; foliar K is not a mandatory quick fix.
Use appropriate test, crop and local recommendation after conditions improve; no fixed low rate.
Avoid fertiliser application into standing water; reassess roots and plant recovery first.
Choose soil or labelled foliar placement for a verified need, considering uptake, runoff and crop safety.

The teaching case names organic matter for structure and subsurface tile drainage as long-term examples. They require site-specific assessment and design, not an automatic cure or permission to excavate.
Drainage/root oxygen is the first problem to investigate; K is a testable secondary hypothesis.

sourceBindings.text: Case 3: leafy crop planning on loam
A leafy crop is planned in loam with limited water; the card describes planning, not an existing deficiency symptom.
Drip may distribute limited water near rows if equipment and maintenance are feasible.
Nitrogen demand may be substantial, but no deficiency or rate is established.
Identify crop and stage, local ET and effective rainfall, root-zone storage, system suitability, water quality and a valid nutrient test.
Compare costs and maintenance; check fertilizer product analysis.
Consider a designed, monitored drip system; no blanket weekly or twice-weekly irrigation cycle.

sourceBindings.text: Case 4: purple young maize in cold clay
Young maize shows purple leaves and slow growth during a cold spring on heavy clay.
Restricted P uptake from cold/wet soil or limited rooting may cause the sign even if soil P is adequate.
A true soil P deficiency or another cause remains possible.
Assess temperature, drainage, root growth, relevant soil P test and whether the crop improves as the soil warms.
Do not add water automatically to a cold wet clay soil; check moisture and drainage first.
DAP or monoammonium phosphate (MAP) are possible P-source examples only if agronomic need and product suitability are confirmed.
Use test and local crop guidance, not a vague 'modest' dose.
Plan when P is needed and field conditions permit safe application; avoid an unexamined immediate remedy.

A safe band near young roots can be appropriate, with product-specific separation from the seed and no universal superiority over every alternative. This teaching example illustrates an at-planting starter band 2 inches to the side and 2 inches below the seed row. This is a placement example, not a universal setting or an instruction to dig beside established seedlings. Actual placement must follow the product, crop, equipment and local seed-safety guidance.
Test the P hypothesis and soil conditions before a four-part fertilizer recommendation.

sourceBindings.text: Caso 1: pomodori su sabbia
Terreno sabbioso caldo e ventoso con irrigazione superficiale; pomodori sani al mattino ma appassiti al pomeriggio, foglie vecchie pallide o gialle.
La domanda diurna può superare temporaneamente l’assorbimento; poca riserva radicale o irrigazione a scorrimento non controllata possono contribuire.
Il giallo sulle foglie vecchie suggerisce carenza mobile di N o K, lisciviazione, problemi radicali o altro.
Controlla umidità radicale mattina/pomeriggio, radici, drenaggio, ultimo turno irriguo, meteo e fattibilità del goccia.
Ottieni analisi del suolo/tessuti e fase colturale prima di scegliere concime.

Valuta un impianto a goccia filtrato e mantenibile al posto di apporti superficiali incontrollati, misurandone il funzionamento; non prescrivere acqua ogni giorno dal solo aspetto. La distribuzione vicino alle radici evita la deriva del getto in aria, può ridurre evaporazione dal suolo e bagnatura delle infestanti tra le file e mantenere più asciutte le foglie, riducendo alcuni rischi di malattia. Piccoli apporti monitorati possono adattarsi alla limitata riserva della sabbia, ma l’eccesso può ancora scendere sotto le radici; i vantaggi dipendono da progetto, gestione e condizioni.
Scegli la fonte adatta al pomodoro solo dopo prove; un prodotto solubile bilanciato è una classe possibile, non una diagnosi.
Usa risultati, domanda colturale, disponibilità esistente e guida locale; il colore non fornisce dose.
Conferma domanda e rischio di perdite; fertirrigare ogni turno o a turni alterni non è automatico.
Se la fertirrigazione è giustificata, usa erogazione radicale autorizzata e controlla lisciviazione e uniformità.
Il modello parla di una classe di concime per pomodori in fruttificazione. Conferma la fase reale; la domanda del banco da sola non determina l’analisi del prodotto.
Distingui ipotesi su caldo/acqua e nutrienti, verifica entrambe e poi scegli acqua e 4R condizionate.

sourceBindings.text: Caso 3: verdura a foglia su franco
Si pianifica una coltura a foglia su franco con poca acqua; la scheda riguarda la pianificazione, non sintomi di carenza già osservati.
Il goccia può distribuire acqua vicino alle file se kit e manutenzione sono fattibili.
La domanda di N può essere rilevante, ma nessuna carenza o dose è dimostrata.
Identifica coltura e fase, evapotraspirazione locale e pioggia efficace, riserva idrica nella zona radicale, idoneità del sistema, qualità dell'acqua e un'analisi valida dei nutrienti.
Confronta costo/manutenzione e analisi del prodotto.
Valuta un impianto a goccia progettato e controllato; nessun ciclo irriguo settimanale o due volte alla settimana valido per tutti.
Una formula NPK completa solo se il piano richiede N, P e K. Il nitrato di calcio dà N e Ca, non è NPK bilanciato.
Deriva da coltura, analisi e guida locale, non solo da «poco e spesso».
Adegua alle fasi e domanda misurata; fertirrigare ogni settimana o due non è universale.
Se prodotto solubile approvato e impianto lo consentono, distribuisci alle radici con goccia verificato; altrimenti usa alternativa idonea.
Pianificazione preventiva: non inventare carenza diagnosticata né calendario fisso.

sourceBindings.text: Caso 4: mais giovane viola su argilla fredda
Mais giovane viola e lento in una primavera fredda su terreno argilloso pesante.
Freddo/ristagno o poche radici possono frenare P anche se l’analisi del suolo è adeguata.
Vera carenza di P o altra causa resta possibile.
Controlla temperatura, drenaggio, radici, analisi P pertinente e miglioramento con il riscaldamento.
Non aggiungere acqua automaticamente a un’argilla fredda e bagnata; controlla umidità e drenaggio.
DAP o fosfato monoammonico (MAP) sono esempi possibili di fonte P solo con bisogno agronomico e compatibilità del prodotto confermati.
Dose da analisi e guida locale, non da «modesta» indefinita.
Intervieni quando serve e il campo consente sicurezza, non subito senza indagine.

Banda vicino alle giovani radici possibile con separazione dal seme prevista dall’etichetta, non superiore sempre alle alternative. Questo esempio didattico illustra alla semina una banda starter a 2 pollici di lato e 2 pollici sotto la fila dei semi. È un esempio di posizionamento, non un’impostazione universale né un invito a scavare accanto a piantine già insediate. Il posizionamento reale segue prodotto, coltura, attrezzatura e indicazioni locali per la sicurezza del seme.

sourceBindings.text: Fall 2: kümmernder Weizen auf nassem Ton
Nach starkem Regen steht Wasser auf Ton; Weizen ist klein, einige ältere Blattränder vergilben.
Staunässe begrenzt Sauerstoff an Wurzeln und damit Wasser- und Nährstoffaufnahme.

sourceBindings.text: Fall 3: Blattgemüse-Planung auf Lehm
Eine Blattkultur wird auf Lehm mit begrenztem Wasser geplant; die Karte schildert Planung, keine bestehenden Mangelzeichen.
Tropfbewässerung kann wenig Wasser in Reihen verteilen, wenn Technik und Wartung passen.
N-Bedarf kann hoch sein, doch weder Mangel noch Menge sind festgestellt.
Kultur/Phase, lokale ET, wirksamen Regen, Wurzelspeicher, System/Wasserqualität und gültigen Nährstofftest ermitteln.
Kosten/Wartung und Produktanalyse vergleichen.
Eine geplante und überwachte Tropfanlage erwägen; keinen pauschalen wöchentlichen oder zweimal wöchentlichen Bewässerungszyklus festlegen.
Vollständiges NPK nur, wenn der Plan N, P und K fordert. Calciumnitrat enthält N und Ca, ist kein ausgewogenes NPK.
Aus Kultur, Analyse und lokaler Vorgabe statt bloß „wenig und oft“ ableiten.
Nach Wachstum und gemessenem Bedarf; wöchentliche/zweiwöchentliche Fertigation nicht allgemein.
Bei freigegebenem löslichem Produkt und passender Anlage über geprüfte Tropfer zur Wurzelzone; sonst geeignete Alternative.
Vorausschauende Planung, ohne Mangel oder festen Wasser-/Düngeplan zu erfinden.

sourceBindings.text: Fall 4: purpurner Jungmais auf kaltem Ton
Jungmais mit Purpurblättern und langsamem Wachstum im kalten Frühjahr auf schwerem Ton.
Kälte, Nässe oder schwache Wurzeln können P-Aufnahme trotz ausreichendem Bodengehalt hemmen.
Echter P-Mangel oder eine andere Ursache bleibt möglich.
Temperatur, Entwässerung, Wurzelwachstum, passenden P-Test und Besserung beim Erwärmen prüfen.
Kalten nassen Ton nicht automatisch weiter gießen; Feuchte und Abfluss zuerst prüfen.
DAP oder Monoammoniumphosphat (MAP) sind mögliche Beispiele für P-Quellen, sofern Bedarf und Produkteignung bestätigt sind.
Nach Analyse und lokaler Kulturberatung, nicht pauschal „mäßig“.
Bei Bedarf und sicheren Feldbedingungen, nicht ungeprüft sofort.

Sicheres Band neben jungen Wurzeln nach etikettgerechtem Saatabstand möglich, nicht immer allen Alternativen überlegen. Dieses Lehrbeispiel zeigt ein Starterband bei der Aussaat 2 Zoll seitlich und 2 Zoll unterhalb der Saatreihe. Das ist ein Platzierungsbeispiel, keine allgemeine Einstellung und keine Anweisung, neben bereits etablierten Jungpflanzen zu graben. Die tatsächliche Platzierung richtet sich nach Produkt, Kultur, Gerät und örtlichen Vorgaben zum Schutz des Saatguts.
P-Hypothese und Bodenverhältnisse vor der vierteiligen Empfehlung prüfen.
